### Rounders (1998) — Strategy, Loyalty & The Cost of Risk ♠️

Rounders is a crime drama starring Matt Damon as Mike McDermott, a gifted poker player who believes he has what it takes to succeed at the highest levels. After losing his savings in a high-stakes game, Mike decides to leave gambling behind and focus on building a more stable future.

But when his longtime friend Worm, played by Edward Norton, returns with dangerous debts and trouble following him, Mike finds himself drawn back into the underground poker world. With powerful players watching and the pressure mounting, he must use his intelligence, patience, and ability to read people to survive.

The movie explores friendship, ambition, temptation, and calculated risk. It reveals how one decision can change everything and how confidence can become dangerous when pride takes control.

What makes Rounders stand out is its intense poker scenes and psychological battles. Every hand tests the characters' ability to stay calm, recognize an opponent's weakness, and know when to take a chance.

💬 “The real skill isn't just knowing how to win—it's knowing what you're willing to lose.”

source_details.synopsis: Rounders is a 1998 American crime drama film about the underground world of high-stakes poker, directed by John Dahl and starring Matt Damon and Edward Norton. The story follows two friends who need to win at high-stakes poker to quickly pay off a large debt. The term "rounder" refers to a person traveling around from city to city seeking high-stakes card games. Rounders premiered at the Venice Film Festival on September 4, 1998, and was theatrically released in the United States on September 11.
